slot.brief: A particle at a given position with given velocity experiences a force; compute torque r × F and angular momentum r × mv about origin and check their relation.

stem: At an instant, a particle of mass $3$ kg has position $\mathbf r=(2,-1,1)$ m and velocity $\mathbf v=(1,2,0)$ m s$^{-1}$. The net force is $\mathbf F=(2,1,-1)$ N. Which ordered pair gives its angular momentum and torque about the origin, respectively?

verdicts.working: \(\mathbf L=\mathbf r\times m\mathbf v=3(\mathbf r\times\mathbf v)=(-6,3,15)\). \(\boldsymbol\tau=\mathbf r\times\mathbf F=(0,4,4)\).

working:
$\mathbf L=\mathbf r\times m\mathbf v=(2,-1,1)\times(3,6,0)=(-6,3,15)\ \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$
$\boldsymbol\tau=\mathbf r\times\mathbf F=(2,-1,1)\times(2,1,-1)=(0,4,4)\ \text{N m}$
$\dfrac{d\mathbf L}{dt}=\mathbf r\times\mathbf F+\mathbf v\times m\mathbf v=\boldsymbol\tau$

Independent check: \(\mathbf L=\mathbf r\times m\mathbf v=3(\mathbf r\times\mathbf v)=(-6,3,15)\). \(\boldsymbol\tau=\mathbf r\times\mathbf F=(0,4,4)\).
solution:
Angular momentum and torque about the origin are $4\mathbf L=\mathbf r\times m\mathbf v,\qquad \boldsymbol\tau=\mathbf r\times\mathbf F.4$
$$\mathbf L=(2,-1,1)\times(3,6,0)=(-6,3,15),\qquad \boldsymbol\tau=(2,-1,1)\times(2,1,-1)=(0,4,4).$$
Thus the ordered pair is $\bigl((-6,3,15)\ \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1},(0,4,4)\ \text{N m}\bigr)$.
